input.objective:
Launch Pondside (POND) with a Uniswap v4 hook on Sepolia, paired with ETH.
Token: Pondside (POND), the standard launch token: 1,000,000,000 supply, 18 decimals, plain transfers, no owner functions.
The hook does exactly the following, and nothing else:
1. Take 0.5% of the ETH side of every buy and 2.0% of the ETH side of every sell as a hook fee, settled in ETH inside the swap that paid it (mint a claim when the PoolManager cannot pay it directly), and send it to my wallet. Expose claimFees() that anyone may call to redeem claims to the recipient.
2. Liquidity added to the pool is locked for 7 days from the time it was added; removing it earlier reverts. The launch factory’s own zero-change fee collection is always allowed. Expose unlockAt(address) as a view.
3. Penalize just-in-time liquidity: liquidity removed within 10 blocks of being added forfeits the fees it earned in that time to the remaining liquidity providers (the LiquidityPenaltyHook pattern).
4. Only addresses the owner has added to a liquidity allowlist may add liquidity; anyone may remove their own. The launch factory’s initial seeding is always allowed. Expose setLpAllowed(address[] accounts, bool allowed) for the owner and isLpAllowed(address) as a view.
5. Reject adding liquidity worth less than 0.05 ETH at the current price. Removing is never blocked by this rule.
6. Reject every swap before 2026-11-01 16:00 UTC. Liquidity may be added before then. Expose opensAt() as a view.
7. Allow swaps only between 9:00 and 17:00 UTC each day, judged by block timestamp; reject all others. Liquidity changes are always allowed. Expose isOpen() as a view.
8. For the first 15 minutes after the pool opens, only addresses the owner has added to an allowlist may buy. After that, anyone. Expose setAllowed(address[] accounts, bool allowed) for the owner and isAllowed(address) as a view.
9. The owner may pause and unpause swaps. Liquidity can always be removed while paused. Expose pause() and unpause() for the owner and paused() as a view.
10. After 2027-01-01 00:00 UTC every rule above stops applying and the hook lets every swap and liquidity change through unchanged, forever. Expose sunsetAt() as a view.
11. Record a time-weighted average price of the pool that other contracts can read (the BaseOracleHook pattern, with a Uniswap v3 compatible observe interface). Expose twap(uint32 secondsAgo) as a view returning the average price as a Q64.96 sqrt price.
12. Let users place limit orders in the hook that fill automatically when the pool price crosses the order price, and withdraw unfilled orders at any time (the LimitOrderHook pattern). Expose placeOrder(bool zeroForOne, int24 tick, uint256 amount) returning an id, cancelOrder(uint256 id) and claim(uint256 id).
13. Liquidity the pool is not using at the current price is lent on Aave and recalled when needed for swaps (the ReHypothecationHook pattern). If Aave has no deployment on the chosen chain, the swarm must report that as a blocker instead of substituting another protocol. Expose rebalance() that anyone may call.
14. Donations to the pool are allowed from only the owner; all other donations revert. Expose setDonor(address account, bool allowed) for the owner.
Owner the paying wallet may only: add and remove liquidity-provider allowlist addresses, add and remove buyer allowlist addresses, pause and unpause swaps, change the donation allowlist, through the functions named above. No other admin function, no backend signer, no upgrade path.
Fees are always taken from the ETH (pair currency) side, never from POND; a fee the PoolManager cannot pay directly is minted as a claim the recipient can redeem.
Enable beforeInitialize (required by the IMD launch factory) and only the callbacks the behavior above needs. Take the PoolManager as a constructor argument. Owner, if any, is $owner.
Pool: 50% of my 90% share seeds the pool; the remainder goes to the paying wallet.
Keep the function names exactly as written so the storefront can show them. Composed with The Hooks Store block builder.
